## Just Cause Eviction Requirements

**Status:** Enacted

RETRIEVED: 2026-10-01 22:37 UTC

Overview of Just Cause Evictions | SF.gov
Skip to main content

Overview of Just Cause Evictions
In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
Rent Board
In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

content.text: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

citations.cited_text: Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

content.text: The mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

The just cause reasons include: non-payment of rent; failure to cure substantial breach; nuisance; illegal use; refusal to renew agreement; refusal to allow access; unapproved subtenancy; owner-occupancy; condominium conversion sale; unit demolition; capital improvements; substantial rehabilitation; Ellis Act withdrawal; lead remediation; demolition under development agreement; expired "Good Samaritan" tenancy (within 60 days); and completion of development projects requiring demolition.

citations.cited_text:
The landlord also needs a "just cause“ reason to take away or remove access to certain
housing services
, including but not limited to garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms.

content.text: A landlord needs "just cause" to remove access to housing services including garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms.

citations.cited_text:
However, a landlord who has complied with the requirements of Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may
temporarily remove certain housing services
, including parking and storage spaces, in order to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work required by
the Building Code
.

content.text: a landlord who has complied with Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove certain housing services for mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work.
**Exemptions from Rent Increase Limitations (but subject to just cause eviction):**

citations.cited_text:
Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance. This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies that are eligible for a rent increase under the
Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act,
and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.

content.text: Some tenancies exempt from rent increase limitations are still subject to eviction provisions and can only be evicted for "just cause" reasons, including tenancies in newly constructed units with Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, those eligible under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some where rent is regulated by another government agency.
